run.question: My AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 has high latency issues. Investigate why.

report.summary: I could not find any evidence about an AWS Lambda function named 'payment-processor' in us-east-1: this Run has no AWS/CloudWatch, CloudWatch Logs or Logs Insights source configured (available sources are Jaeger, Kubernetes, Prometheus and the runbook knowledge base; change_history is listed as not integrated), and no Lambda-named or AWS-named workload exists in the queried Kubernetes cluster. The only similarly named entity is a different one: Deployment 'payment' (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) in namespace otel-demo, which I checked as a related-but-different entity. It is Running and Ready, its Service (10.96.116.236:8080) and its Endpoints (10.244.0.5 -> payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d) are consistent, and its application logs from 2026-11-22T08:21:22Z to 08:50:41Z show paired 'Charge request received'/'Transaction complete' lines with no error lines; the only restart marks are an exit code 255 with reason 'Unknown' at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z that coincided with Normal 'SandboxChanged' events on every otel-demo pod at 08:04:18Z. The latency signals that would answer the question (traces and histogram/error-rate metrics for payment) could not be read at all: every Prometheus and Jaeger tool call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no latency value, trend or baseline exists in this Run and I make no latency claim in either direction. Runbook lambda-performance-troubleshooting (skill_id lambda-performance-troubleshooting) was fetched: Step 1 (CloudWatch Duration) and Step 3 (InitDuration) could not be carried out — no CloudWatch tool; Step 4 (ConcurrentExecutions) could not be carried out — same missing integration; Step 2 (CloudWatch Logs error extraction) could not be carried out — no CloudWatch Logs source, though I read the Kubernetes pod logs of the different, related 'payment' deployment and found no error lines; Step 5 (Logs Insights memory stats) could not be carried out — no Logs Insights source.

claims.text: Only one pod in the whole cluster matches 'lambda|payment|aws' in name, labels or image: payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d in namespace otel-demo with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment; no Lambda-named workload appears.
The cluster's namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly and otel-demo; no AWS/Lambda-specific namespace exists.
All 21 deployments in namespace otel-demo report 1 desired and 1 available replica; the payment deployment runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment.
Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running with container ready=true, restartCount=2 and startTime 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z, i.e. older than the incident window.
The payment container's last termination was exitCode 255 with reason 'Unknown', startedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z and finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z; the reason is 'Unknown', not OOMKilled.

Normal events 'Pod sandbox changed, it will be killed and re-created' (SandboxChanged) were recorded at 2026-11-22T08:04:18Z for essentially every otel-demo pod, including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, followed by Pulled/Created/Started at 08:04:19-08:04:20Z for the payment pod.

Payment pod logs between 2026-11-22T08:21:22Z and 08:50:41Z (newest 100 of 155 matching lines, current container instance) show repeated pairs of 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.' with the same trace_id tens of milliseconds apart (e.g. 08:21:22.966 -> 08:21:22.967, 08:50:41.050 -> 08:50:41.051), and no failure lines.

A log search over the same payment pod for err|fail|timeout|exception|warn|slow|latency matched only 2 lines, both a Node.js metadata warning at 2026-11-22T08:04:24.937Z ('MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header') and its '(Use `node --trace-warnings ...`)' hint; 153 lines of 155 read were removed by the filter.

ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) declares payment-related fault flags paymentFailure (variants 100/90/75/50/25/10/off) and paymentUnreachable (on/off), and both have defaultVariant 'off'; every other flag in the file (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) also has defaultVariant 'off', and no flag injects latency into the payment service.

Deployment payment is at generation 1 with replicas=1, readyReplicas=1, updatedReplicas=1, condition NewReplicaSetAvailable lastTransitionTime 2026-11-20T16:33:03Z and pod template image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment; no rollout or template change occurred inside the incident window.

Service 'payment' exposes clusterIP 10.96.116.236 port 8080/tcp-service to targetPort 8080 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment, and its Endpoints object lists address 10.244.0.5 with targetRef Pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, so the service-to-pod wiring is consistent.

Pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (container nginx) shows restartCount=6 with lastState terminated exitCode=1 reason=Error finishedAt 2026-11-22T08:04:42Z and is currently Ready, and its events include 4 BackOff plus probe-failure 'connection refused' Unhealthy events between 08:04:23Z and 08:05:10Z; prometheus-9bc78b5f7-c9wx8 also restarted with exitCode 255 reason Unknown at 08:04:13Z and is currently Ready.

The only other pods with probe/restart trouble in the event window are kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz (liveness/readiness 'connection refused', 3 each, container killed by liveness probe) and otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c (readiness probe 'connection refused' x3) — these are monitoring-plane pods, not the payment workload.

Evidence against a payment-service latency problem in the related (different-entity) Kubernetes Deployment payment: its request logs show complete transactions and no error/slow lines, its deployment was not rolled out during the window, its Service selector matches its only endpoint, and the payment fault flags are off.

Rejected: the payment container's restart was an OOM kill or crash cause of latency. The last termination reason is 'Unknown' with exitCode 255 (not OOMKilled), the restart coincides with a cluster-wide 'SandboxChanged' recreation of all otel-demo pods at 08:04:18Z, the deployment template was unchanged (generation 1), and the pod's own logs after restart contain no failures — the restart is a mechanism of the runtime change, not evidence of payment latency.

Rejected as a cause inside this cluster: an enabled flagd fault-injection flag against payment. paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are declared but both have defaultVariant 'off', and no payment-targeted latency flag exists in demo.flagd.json.

Rejected as a cause: payment Service/Endpoints misconfiguration. The Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment resolves to one ready endpoint 10.244.0.5 = pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d on port 8080, so there is no empty or mismatched endpoint set.

The subject of the question is likely outside the observed system: 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 would be an AWS Lambda function, and nothing in this Run's sources (Kubernetes cluster plus Prometheus and Jaeger for the otel-demo target) contains it. The Kubernetes Deployment 'payment' is proposed only as a similarly named but different entity, not as the same function; the identity is not verified.

Unverified: the crash-looping prometheus-readonly-proxy (nginx restartCount=6, BackOff x4, probe 'connection refused' at 08:04:23-08:05:10Z) may be why every Prometheus query in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE; Jaeger also returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE although its pod was recreated normally, so a single proxy fault does not explain both, and the cause of the tool unavailability is not established.

To answer the Lambda latency question, query AWS CloudWatch for the function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 (Duration p50/p99, InitDuration for cold starts, ConcurrentExecutions, Errors/Throttles) and CloudWatch Logs for timeouts and slow-handler lines, and compare against a pre-incident baseline; the runbook's steps 1-5 are exactly those checks and none could be executed here because no AWS/CloudWatch source is integrated.

content.name: lambda-performance-troubleshooting
content.content:
# AWS Lambda High Latency Troubleshooting

## Overview
This runbook helps diagnose and resolve AWS Lambda function performance issues including high latency, timeouts, and cold starts.

## Steps

### Step 1: Query Performance Metrics
Use CloudWatch to check Lambda function latency over time:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name Duration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 2: Check Function Logs
Look for errors or slow operations in CloudWatch Logs:
```bash
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --filter-pattern "[ERROR] OR [WARN] OR timeout" --limit 100
```

### Step 3: Analyze Cold Start Patterns
Query CloudWatch for cold start frequency:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name InitDuration --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Average,Count --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 300
```

### Step 4: Check Concurrent Executions
Verify Lambda isn't hitting concurrency limits:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace <lambda-namespace> \
  --metric-name ConcurrentExecutions --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=<function-name> \
  --statistics Maximum --start-time <start-time> \
  --end-time <end-time> --period 60
```

### Step 5: Review Memory Utilization
Check if function needs more memory allocation:
```bash
aws logs insights start-query --log-group-name <lambda-log-group>/<function-name> \
  --start-time <epoch-start> --end-time <epoch-end> \
  --query-string "fields @timestamp, @message | filter @type = 'REPORT' | stats max(@maxMemoryUsed), avg(@memorySize)"
```
